entry: Conflict (1808–1814) in which Spain, Portugal and the United Kingdom fought the occupying forces of the [[First French Empire]] during the [[Napoleonic Wars]]. After [[Napoleon]] placed his brother Joseph on the Spanish throne, most Spaniards rejected French rule and fought a guerrilla war. Spanish forces defeated the French at the Battle of Bailén in [[Andalusia]] in 1808. British troops under Arthur Wellesley, later Duke of Wellington, fought alongside the Portuguese, and allied armies defeated the French at Salamanca (1812) and Vitoria (1813). The French withdrew across the [[Pyrenees]] in 1813–1814. The Spanish Constitution of 1812 later became a cornerstone of European [[Liberalism|liberalism]].

Male sexual organ used to inseminate females during copulation, found in many [[Animal|animals]]. Penises occur in both [[Vertebrate|vertebrates]] and invertebrates, but not every species has one, and they are not necessarily homologous. The term does not cover every intromittent organ: most [[Cephalopod|cephalopods]] use a modified arm, and male spiders use their pedipalps. In most species the organ does little beyond intromission or conveying sperm. In [[Mammal|placental mammals]], however, it contains the distal part of the [[Urethra|urethra]], which discharges both urine and [[Semen|semen]]. Most male birds have no penis, but paleognaths such as the [[Tinamou|tinamous]] and waterfowl have one; the bird penis is erected by lymph rather than blood. The lake duck has the longest penis of any vertebrate relative to its body length.

U.S. state in the Mid-Atlantic and Great Lakes regions (pop., 2020: over 13 million). It is the fifth-most populous state and the 33rd largest by land area. Its largest metropolitan area is centered on [[Philadelphia]], the state's most populous city, and [[Pittsburgh]] is the second-largest city; the capital is Harrisburg. The [[Appalachian Mountains]] run through the center of the state, and about 59% of the land is forested. Pennsylvania has 140 miles (225 km) of waterfront along [[Lake Erie]] and the tidal Delaware River. Founded in 1681 through a royal land grant to William Penn, it was known for religious tolerance and relatively peaceful relations with native tribes. Philadelphia hosted the First and Second Continental Congresses, and Pennsylvania was the second state to ratify the U.S. Constitution, on December 12, 1787. In the 21st century it has been nicknamed the Cellicon State for the role of Philadelphia and Pittsburgh in technology and cancer immunotherapy.

American actress, director and producer. Born in [[Manhattan]], she played Laverne DeFazio on the sitcom *Laverne & Shirley* from 1976 to 1983, earning three Golden Globe nominations for the role. She made her directorial debut with *Jumpin' Jack Flash* (1986). Her film *Big* (1988) became the first film directed by a woman to gross more than $100 million at the U.S. box office. Her later directing credits include *Awakenings* (1990), nominated for the Academy Award for Best Picture, and *A League of Their Own* (1992). She also produced *Cinderella Man* and *Bewitched* (both 2005).

Fund or scheme that pays regular income to a person after retirement. Contributions are made during working life by employees, employers, governments or other sources. In a defined benefit plan, payments are fixed and contributions are adjusted to fund them; in a defined contribution plan, contributions are fixed and retirement payments depend on what the fund can afford. Pensions differ from severance pay, which is typically a one-time payment after involuntary termination. Retirement plans may be set up by employers, [[Insurance|insurance companies]], [[Government|governments]] or [[Trade union|trade unions]]. They are called retirement plans in the [[United States]], pension schemes in the [[United Kingdom]], and superannuation plans in Australia and [[New Zealand]]. Occupational pensions are a form of deferred compensation and often pay benefits to survivors or disabled beneficiaries. The Roman emperor [[Augustus]] established a military treasury in 6 AD to pay retiring legionnaires.

Regular five-pointed star polygon formed from the diagonals of a regular pentagon. Also called a pentalpha or star pentagon, it is an ancient symbol. Early pentagrams appear on Sumerian pottery from [[Ur]] (c. 3500 BC), and Pythagoreans of the 6th century BC used it as a badge of recognition. In the Serer religion of the Serer people in [[Senegal]], Gambia and [[Mauritania]], the pentagram is the symbol of the Universe. A circle drawn around its points forms the pentacle, which is widely used by [[Wicca|Wiccans]] and in [[Paganism|paganism]].

Renewal movement within evangelical Protestant Christianity that emphasizes direct personal experience of God through baptism with the Holy Spirit. The name derives from Pentecost, when the Holy Spirit descended on Jesus's followers in Jerusalem, as described in Acts 2. Like other [[Evangelicalism|evangelicals]], Pentecostals hold the [[Bible]] to be inerrant and believe in being born again, but they also teach a baptism in the Holy Spirit, evidenced by speaking in tongues. The three-year-long Azusa Street Revival, led by William J. Seymour in [[Los Angeles]], [[California]], spread the movement worldwide. The movement comprises over 700 denominations and is highly decentralized. Classical Pentecostals number over 279 million, and with the Charismatic movement the total exceeds 644 million, growing fastest in the Global South, including [[Sub-Saharan Africa|sub-Saharan Africa]]. Oneness Pentecostalism, which rejects the [[Trinity]], is one of the non-trinitarian branches.

[[Genus]] of flowering plants, *Paeonia*, native to Asia, Europe and western North America. Estimates of the number of species range from 25 to 40, though the current consensus describes 33 known species. Most are herbaceous perennials 0.25–1 m (1–3 ft) tall, while some are woody shrubs up to 3.5 m (11 ft). Their large, often fragrant flowers range from purple and pink to red, white and yellow, and bloom for only 7–10 days in late spring and early summer. Herbaceous peonies are popular garden plants in temperate regions and are sold on a large scale as cut flowers.

Military wing of the Chinese Communist Party and the primary armed forces of the [[China|People's Republic of China]]. It consists of the Ground Force, Navy, Air Force and Rocket Force, plus four arms, and operates under the absolute control of the party through the Central Military Commission. Since 1989 the party general secretary has also been the commission's chairman. The PLA traces its origins to the Chinese Red Army, formed in 1927 by left-wing units of the [[Kuomintang]]'s National Revolutionary Army, and the communist units were reconstituted as the PLA in 1947. It is the world's largest military force, excluding paramilitary and reserve forces. China's military expenditure was US$336 billion in 2024, accounting for 12 percent of world defense expenditure.

Prehistoric migration of humans from Asia into North and South America. The migration is believed to have begun when Paleolithic hunter-gatherers, known as Paleo-Indians, crossed the Beringia land bridge between northeastern [[Siberia]] and western [[Alaska]], exposed when sea levels fell during the [[Last Glacial Maximum]] (26,000 to 19,000 years ago). Their descendants spread south and occupied both continents no later than 14,000 years ago, and possibly before 20,000 years ago. Indigenous peoples have been linked to Siberian populations through blood types and DNA. The exact date and route remain disputed. The [[Clovis culture]] was long thought to be the earliest human presence, about 13,000 years ago, but sites such as Monte Verde in [[Chile]], dated to 14,500 years ago, challenged this. The oldest undisputed evidence of habitation, at Swan Point in Alaska, has radiocarbon dates of 14,000 years, indicating occupation around 12,000 BC.

Catalan-born Spanish football manager and former defensive midfielder. As a player, he spent most of his career at [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]], where he was part of Johan Cruyff's Dream Team that won the club's first European Cup in 1992; he won 47 caps for Spain. As manager of Barcelona from 2008, he led the club to the continental treble in his first season, and he later won the [[Bundesliga]] with Bayern Munich in each of his three seasons. At Manchester City, which he managed from 2016, he won six [[Premier League]] titles. He is one of only two managers to have won the continental treble twice.

British preschool [[Animation|animated]] television series. Created by Neville Astley and Mark Baker, it follows Peppa, an anthropomorphic [[Pig|piglet]], her family and friends, who are portrayed as other animals. Each episode runs about five minutes and shows everyday activities such as attending playgroup or visiting relatives. The first series began on Channel 5 on 31 May 2004, and the show has been broadcast in over 180 countries. Narrator John Sparkes says "Oh, dear" when something unfortunate happens. In 2019 Hasbro acquired Entertainment One, which included the franchise, for US$3.8 billion.

American multinational food and beverage corporation headquartered in Purchase, New York. Formed in 1965 through the merger of the Pepsi-Cola Company and Frito-Lay, it expanded from its flagship drink, [[Pepsi]], into a range of food and beverage brands. Acquisitions included Tropicana Products (1998) and the Quaker Oats Company (2001), which added Gatorade. As of January 2021 it had 23 brands with annual sales above $1 billion each. It is the second-largest food and beverage business in the world, behind [[Nestlé]]. The company has faced criticism over deforestation, [[Pesticide|pesticide]] residue and plastic pollution; in 2024 it was the second-highest producer of branded plastic pollution globally.

Cola-flavored carbonated [[Soft drink|soft drink]], the flagship product of [[PepsiCo]]. Caleb Bradham created it in 1893 as "Brad's Drink" in New Bern, [[North Carolina]], and renamed it Pepsi-Cola in 1898. The company went bankrupt in 1923 but was revived by Charles Guth, who reformulated the syrup. Its popularity grew during the [[Great Depression]] with a 12-ounce bottle and the "Nickel, Nickel" jingle, which doubled sales. Its rivalry with [[Coca-Cola]] in the "cola wars" produced the "Pepsi Challenge" taste tests and the introduction of New Coke in response. In 2023 Pepsi was the second most valuable soft drink brand worldwide, behind Coca-Cola.

Short chain of [[Amino acid|amino acids]], typically 2–50 residues long, linked by peptide bonds. Chains of fewer than twenty amino acids are called oligopeptides, including dipeptides and tripeptides. A polypeptide with a molecular mass of 10,000 Da or more is called a [[Protein|protein]]. Peptides are usually linear, with a free amine at the N-terminus and a carboxyl group at the C-terminus. Many ribosomal peptides act as [[Hormone|hormones]] or signaling molecules, and some microbes produce peptides as [[Antibiotic|antibiotics]]. Nonribosomal peptides are assembled by enzymes rather than by the [[Ribosome|ribosome]]; glutathione, a component of antioxidant defenses, is a common example.

Order of [[Marsupial|marsupials]] comprising the bandicoots and bilbies, endemic to [[Australia]] and [[New Guinea]]. Most have the characteristic bandicoot shape: a plump, arch-backed body with a long, tapering snout, very large upright ears, and relatively long, thin legs. They range from about 140 g to 4 kg, but most species weigh about one kilogram. Its placement among marsupials is controversial. Its polyprotodont teeth suggest a link with [[Dasyuromorphia|carnivorous marsupials]], while its syndactylous hind feet resemble those of the [[Diprotodontia|diprotodonts]]. Molecular studies place the order at a distant remove from other marsupial orders. Fossil bandicoots are known from the [[Pleistocene]] and [[Holocene]].

Number or ratio expressed as a fraction of 100, from [[Latin]] *per centum*, meaning "by a hundred". Denoted with the percent sign (%), it is a dimensionless number used mainly to express proportions. For example, 45% is 45/100, or 0.45. Percentages are not restricted to values between 0 and 100; percent changes of 111% or −35% are common. A ratio is converted by multiplying it by 100, so 50 is 4% of 1,250. Percentages of percentages are found by multiplying the fractions: 50% of 40% is 20%. In [[Ancient Rome]], [[Augustus]] levied a tax of 1/100 on goods sold at auction, and by the 17th century interest rates were commonly quoted in hundredths.

Common name for freshwater fish of the genus *Perca* in the family Percidae, order [[Perciformes]]. Perch have long, round bodies, ctenoid scales, and two dorsal fins, the first spiny and the second soft. Three species are recognized. The European perch (*P. fluviatilis*) is found in Europe and has been introduced to [[New Zealand]] and Australia, where it is called redfin perch. The Balkhash perch (*P. schrenkii*) occurs in Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan and [[China]]. The yellow perch (*P. flavescens*) of [[North America]] is smaller and paler than the European species and typically reaches 38 cm (15 in) and 1 kg (2 lb 3 oz). The earliest fossil remains of *Perca* are from the Middle Miocene of Ukraine.

Order of ray-finned fishes in the clade Percomorpha, whose name means "perch-like". It includes [[Perch|perches]] and darters (Percidae) and sea basses (Serranidae), along with many freshwater and marine fish groups. It also contains [[Extremophile|extremophiles]] that have colonized both the North and South Poles and the deepest parts of the ocean. Formerly thought to contain about 41% of bony fish, around 10,000 species in about 160 families, the order has been reduced as many families were moved to other orders within Percomorpha. The earliest fossil perciform, *Paleoserranus*, is from the Early Paleocene of [[Mexico]]. Molecular phylogenetics has clarified its classification, which was long controversial.

Musical instrument sounded by being struck or scraped with a beater, or struck or rubbed by hand. Percussion is not a systematic category of instruments, as its members belong to the idiophone, membranophone, aerophone and chordophone classes. Believed to include the oldest musical instruments, excluding the human voice, percussion can provide [[Rhythm|rhythm]], [[Melody|melody]] and [[Harmony|harmony]]. An [[Orchestra|orchestral]] percussion section commonly includes timpani, snare drum, bass drum, tambourine, [[Cymbal|cymbals]] and triangle. Pitched instruments such as the [[Xylophone|xylophone]] and glockenspiel are included, while keyboard instruments such as the celesta are not normally part of the section.

English Romantic poet and political radical. Shelley did not achieve fame in his lifetime, but his reputation grew after his death, and he influenced [[Thomas Hardy]] and [[W. B. Yeats]]. His best-known works include the verse drama *Prometheus Unbound* (1820), the long poem *Adonais* (1821) and the short poem "Ode to the West Wind" (1819). Much of his work was published posthumously or in expurgated form because of the risk of prosecution for libel. From the 1820s his poems were popular in radical circles, and admirers included [[Karl Marx]] and [[Mahatma Gandhi]]. He lived in self-exile in Italy from 1818. His second wife, [[Mary Shelley]], wrote *Frankenstein*. He died in a boating accident.

Large, crow-sized [[Bird of prey|bird of prey]] of the family Falconidae, known for its speed. It has a blue-grey back, barred white underparts and a black head. Females are considerably larger than males, measuring up to 30% larger. Its breeding range extends from the [[Tundra|Arctic tundra]] to the [[Tropics|tropics]]. The only major ice-free landmass from which it is absent is New Zealand, making it the world's most widespread raptor. Its diet consists almost exclusively of medium-sized birds, and it nests on cliffs or, increasingly, on tall buildings. Pesticides such as [[DDT]] made it [[Endangered species|endangered]] in many areas, but populations recovered after the ban on DDT from the early 1970s.

Positive integer equal to the sum of its proper divisors, which exclude the number itself. The first perfect numbers are 6, 28, 496 and 8128: for example, 1 + 2 + 3 = 6. Equivalently, a perfect number equals its aliquot sum, or half the sum of all its positive divisors. [[Euclid's Elements]] showed that if 2ᵖ − 1 is prime (a [[Mersenne prime]]), then 2ᵖ⁻¹(2ᵖ − 1) is perfect. [[Leonhard Euler]] later proved that all even perfect numbers take this form. It is not known whether any odd perfect numbers exist, nor whether infinitely many perfect numbers exist.

Art form in which the artist's live actions, witnessed in person or through documentation, constitute the work. It involves time, space, the body, the artist's presence and the relation between artist and audience. Its roots lie in [[Futurism|futurist]] productions and cabarets of the 1910s, but the term came into wide use in the 1970s. From the mid-1960s into the 1970s it was defined as an antithesis to theater, drawing on [[Dada]], Fluxus, Viennese Actionism and [[Conceptual art|conceptual art]]. Pioneers include Carolee Schneemann, [[Marina Abramović]], Chris Burden and Joseph Beuys. The works aim to provoke a reaction and often draw on the artist's life experience or social criticism.

Mixture of fragrant essential oils or aroma compounds, fixatives and solvents, used to give bodies, objects and living spaces a pleasant scent. Perfumery began in [[Mesopotamia]], Egypt, the Indus Valley civilization and possibly ancient China, and was refined by the Romans and Muslims. The word derives from Latin *perfumare*, "to smoke through". Tapputi, a perfume maker named on a 2nd-millennium BC [[Cuneiform|cuneiform]] tablet in Mesopotamia, is considered one of the world's first recorded chemists. The Persian chemist [[Avicenna|Ibn Sina]] introduced extraction of flower oils by [[Distillation|distillation]], the procedure most commonly used today. Modern perfumery began in the late 19th century with the synthesis of aroma compounds such as vanillin and coumarin.
